entry.evidence: it remains unclear whether the elastic properties of Cr-pyrope at high P-T can be calculated from the end-member elastic properties

steps.action: Pose the open question: no high-P-T elasticity data exist for Cr-pyrope, and it is unclear whether linear mixing of end-member garnet properties reproduces it.
steps.quote: it remains unclear whether the elastic properties of Cr-pyrope at high P-T can be calculated from the end-member elastic properties

steps.action: Take average Archon, Proton and Tecton SCLM bulk compositions from Griffin et al. (2009) and geotherms from Deen et al. (2006).
steps.quote: The bulk compositions for the Archon, Proton and Tecton were from Griffin et al. (2009)

steps.action: Compute mineral proportions and Cr-pyrope compositions along SCLM geotherms with Perple_X. Use the resulting Uvr+Knr range (4-14 mol.%) to choose a representative sample with 12.2 mol.% Uvr.
steps.quote: it is necessary to know the major element compositional characteristics of the SCLM Cr-pyrope, which helps to choose a proper Cr-pyrope sample to measure

steps.action: Determine the composition of a natural Cr-pyrope from Zhenyuan lamproite (Prp71.0Alm12.6Sps0.7Grs3.5Uvr12.2) by electron microprobe.
steps.quote: Its chemical composition was determined by electron microprobe analysis using a JXA 8230

steps.action: Set laboratory conditions: a diamond anvil cell with Ne medium and ruby gauge up to 11.0 GPa, and an externally heated DAC from room T to 800 K.
steps.quote: The high-T BLS from room T to 800 K (100 K temperature interval) was performed with an externally heated DAC (EHDAC)

steps.action: Collect synchrotron single-crystal XRD for orientation and density, and Brillouin spectra in 10 directions at each P-T point.
steps.quote: BLS spectra were collected at 10 different crystallographic directions from 0 to 90° of the azimuthal angle at every 10°

steps.action: Infer the elastic constants by fitting velocities to the Christoffel equation, then derive VRH aggregate moduli and velocities. Fit third-order finite strain and linear T models for the P and T derivatives, and a BM3 thermal-P EoS to the densities.
steps.quote: were obtained by fitting the corresponding velocity-orientation data to Equation

steps.action: Compare the moduli and derivatives with published BLS and UI values for pyrope and with RPR values for natural Cr-pyropes (Suzuki & Anderson 1983; Babuška et al. 1978).
steps.quote: the compositional variation in natural Cr-pyropes seems to have no significant effect on the room P-T elastic moduli

steps.action: Convert the XRD-EoS isothermal bulk modulus to an adiabatic value and check it against the BLS-measured KS0.
steps.quote: the KS0 calculated from KT0 and the measured KS0 (167.7(8) GPa) show good agreement

steps.action: Compute ρ, KS, G, VP and VS of Prp-Cr#12 at 3-8 GPa and at 1000 and 1600 K two ways: from the directly measured parameters, and from linear mixing of literature end-member parameters (the end-member model).
steps.quote: then compared the results to those calculated using the elastic parameters interpolated from linear mixing of end-member elastic parameters

steps.action: Compare the two calculations: differences of 0.05-2.0% fall within the uncertainties, except for density.
steps.quote: are at the same level as their uncertainties

steps.action: Compute Proton aggregate density and velocities at 3-8 GPa and 1000/1600 K with measured (model#1) versus end-member (model#2) Cr-pyrope parameters.
steps.quote: We calculated the density and velocity of the Proton in two models (model#1 and model#2).

steps.action: Compare model#1 and model#2: differences of 0.05%, 0.03% and 0.1% at 8 GPa and 1600 K are within uncertainties.
steps.quote: using the end-member model elastic parameters of Cr-pyrope has very limited effects on the calculations of density and velocity of the SCLM

steps.action: Keep the end-member model as a sufficient approximation for Cr-pyrope at SCLM conditions.
steps.quote: the end-member model provides a sufficient approximation for the elastic properties of Cr-pyrope at the P-T conditions of the SCLM

steps.action: Model the densities, velocities and ρ/V ratios of Archon, Proton and Tecton at 3-8 GPa and 1300/1500 K, using Perple_X mineralogy and end-member elastic parameters.
steps.quote: we calculated the densities and velocities of the Archon, Proton and Tecton

steps.action: Compare the SCLM types. Density rises from Archon to Tecton (1.1-2.4%), velocity differences are within uncertainty, and ρ/VP and ρ/VS are more sensitive to composition.
steps.quote: indicating that the density of the SCLM increases from Archon to Tecton

steps.action: Refine the comparison to include the ~200 K temperature increase from metasomatism reported in the literature, comparing Archon at 1300 K with Proton and Tecton at 1500 K.
steps.quote: the temperature increase should be considered when we investigate the effects of chemical evolution on the density and velocity of the SCLM

steps.action: Compare the modelled densities with the asthenosphere density profile (Djomani et al. 2001) to discuss delamination, and the velocity drops with the ~1% low-VS anomalies beneath Kaapvaal (Fouch et al. 2004).
steps.quote: the density-P profile of the asthenosphere along 1600 K (Djomani et al., 2001) is shown for comparison.

steps.action: Keep the conclusions: compositional evolution raises SCLM density but not velocity, and ρ/VP and ρ/VS are better indicators of composition.
steps.quote: the chemical evolution of the SCLM from the Archon to the Tecton significantly increases the density of the SCLM

tree.answer: High-P-T elasticity of SCLM Cr-pyrope and validity of linear end-member mixing
No; moduli inferred from Brillouin velocities and XRD densities
Test whether the end-member linear model reproduces measured Cr-pyrope properties
Linear end-member mixing vs non-linearity reported in the literature (rival not computed)
Measured-parameter and end-member-model predictions computed at SCLM P-T
Conditions set in the laboratory (DAC to 11 GPa, EHDAC to 800 K)
One cross-method check (XRD KS0 vs BLS KS0) and literature comparison; single sample
End-member model a sufficient approximation; differences within uncertainty

end.claim: The end-member (linear mixing) model gives a sufficient approximation of Cr-pyrope elastic properties for calculating SCLM density and velocity at SCLM P-T conditions.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the elastic constants, P-T derivatives and EoS inferred from high-P and high-T Brillouin and XRD data on Prp-Cr#12, there would be no measured reference against which to test the end-member model.

gates.evidence: The question about end-member validity and a Perple_X calculation guided the choice of sample composition (p. 3). Data acquisition itself was a standard P-T grid. The test could have failed if differences had exceeded the uncertainties (pp. 9, 11), but those uncertainties (2-3% for KS and G) are large, and the rival was not computed. No hypothesis, threshold or analysis is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Brillouin light scattering with a six-pass tandem Fabry-Pérot interferometer
Single-crystal X-ray diffraction at the Advanced Photon Source 13-BM-D
Diamond anvil cell, externally heated BX90 DAC, ruby pressure gauge, Ne gas loading
Christoffel equation fitted by least squares (Every 1980)
Birch finite-strain theory and third-order Birch-Murnaghan equation of state

novelty_claims.quote: To the best of our knowledge, there is still no elastic property study of Cr-pyrope at high P and high T.
So far, studies on the elastic properties of binary Uvr-Adr or Uvr-Grs solid solutions are unavailable

limits: No review file or earlier version was supplied, so no review sequence is coded; the acknowledgments mention two reviewers and an associate editor. The supporting information (Tables S1-S6, Figures S1-S5, Texts S1-S2) was not supplied, so the end-member parameter set and Figure S4 cannot be checked. Only one natural Cr-pyrope composition was measured: no replication on a second sample and no generalization to other Cr contents. The end-member test is agreement within uncertainties of up to 2-3%, so it has limited power to detect non-linearity (inference). The rival non-linear mixing was not computed. The density difference exceeds its uncertainty but is still judged negligible for aggregates. Sub-claims and their statuses: measured elastic parameters of Prp-Cr#12, estimate_with_resolution. The finding that composition raises SCLM density but not velocity is a forward-model result resting on the end-member model and Perple_X: best_explanation (inference). Gravitational instability and delamination of metasomatized SCLM, and the Kaapvaal low-VS anomaly explained by metasomatic heating, are interpretations not tested: best_explanation at most. Composition is none_fits because the walk is a single-hypothesis laboratory test followed by forward modelling. No rivals share a crucial test, no trace series is involved, and the work does not start from a new capability.

disagreements.quote: However, using the same method, Gwanmesia et al. (2007) and Zou, Irifune, et al. (2012) reported smaller [...]

disagreements.quote: Chen et al. (1999) reported much higher

alternatives_considered.chosen: Third-order Birch-Murnaghan EoS with the Holland & Powell (2011) thermal-pressure model
alternatives_considered.reason: pressure derivative of the bulk modulus of garnet is often larger than 4; Figure 6a shows a good fit

alternatives_considered.chosen: Proton mineralogy at 6 GPa for the model#1/model#2 aggregate test
alternatives_considered.reason: the Cr-pyrope composition at 6 GPa is very close to Prp-Cr#12

alternatives_considered.chosen: Third-order finite strain for olivine and Cr-pyrope moduli; fourth-order for pyroxene bulk moduli and for olivine and pyroxene shear moduli
